title: quest agents --check silently defaults to --target codex, so a Claude-only project checks the wrong file
description: ADR gap 4, at opum-doc main 2112fc6, docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md (operator ruling 2026-09-25T14:09:02.971Z, dispatched by opum-agent as OPAG-421). agents --check with no --target checks AGENTS.md (the codex default, agent-instructions.ts:33, main.ts:1345), so a Claude-only project exits 0 without having checked CLAUDE.md or the Claude skill. The ADR leaves the choice to quest-cli: require --target, pick a smarter default, or document the default as intentional. It must be decided and recorded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The decision (require --target, a smarter default, or a documented intentional default) is recorded with its reasoning on this task
In a Claude-only project, quest agents --check with no --target no longer exits 0 without checking the Claude instructions, or the documented default states exactly what it checks
Help, the guides and the managed block describe the chosen behaviour, and a test covers it

plan: 1. Keep --target codex as the default and refuse the silent case: a bare --check whose AGENTS.md has no Quest block, while CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md carries one, exits 6 (validation) naming the --target to use
2. Correct the agents help text, which lists codex and claude but not antigravity, and state what a bare --check checks
3. Contract test covering Claude-only, codex, both, and an empty project; bun run check
implementationNotes: DECISION (the ADR leaves the choice to quest-cli; recorded here per AC1): keep codex as the default, add a fail-closed refusal, and neither require --target nor infer a target. MEASURED at c76bfc8 on a scratch Claude-only project (init --agent-instructions --target claude): bare `agents --check` exit 0 with instructions.state "missing" (it read AGENTS.md); `--check --require-installed` exit 6 validation "block is missing" (fails, but names no --target); `--check --target claude` exit 0, current. WHY NOT REQUIRE --target: the codex-target managed block itself tells CI to run `quest agents --check --require-installed` with no --target (agent-instructions.ts questAgentInstructionsFor: targetFlag is empty for codex), so requiring it would break every codex workspace CI that follows its own block. WHY NOT INFER A TARGET: help promises one file per invocation, and a check that silently picks which file to check is the same defect in a new place. CHOSEN: a bare --check whose AGENTS.md has no Quest block (state missing), while CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md carries one, exits 6 validation naming the --target to use. Unchanged: codex projects (AGENTS.md has a block), empty projects (nothing anywhere, still missing and exit 0 without --require-installed), and every call that passes --target. Out of scope, not changed: --update-instructions with no --target still writes AGENTS.md, which is its documented behaviour.

IMPLEMENTED in src/cli/main.ts (agents --check). A bare --check whose AGENTS.md is missing a block, while CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md carries one, exits 6 validation. The message names the file that carries the block and the --target to use. The agents help text in main.ts (which omitted antigravity), command-help.ts, and the workspace guide's Managed agent instructions section now state this. That guide also claimed a missing block exits 6; it exits 6 only with --require-installed, and that is corrected. TEST test/qcli373-agents-check-default-target.test.ts has 4 cases: Claude-only and GEMINI-only refuse naming the target, and the explicit --target passes; with both codex and claude, a bare check still reads AGENTS.md; with no block anywhere, it is still missing and exit 0. CONTROL: with main.ts at origin/dev, exactly the 2 refusal cases go red and the 2 unchanged-behaviour cases stay green, as predicted. Two existing contract cases in bootstrap-process.test.ts (QCLI-227, QCLI-159) asserted the old silent exit 0 on a bare check in a Claude-only and a GEMINI-only project. Their stated intent is that each --target checks exactly one file, so they now pass --target codex explicitly. bun run check exit 0, 614 pass. CONSUMER SWEEP, pattern stated: (1) the regex quest[^\n]*agents[^\n]*--check over .github/** at origin/dev in every repo under /Volumes/external/repos. All 9 quest CI invocations (lore-cli, lore-web, opum-agent, opum-cli-e2e, opum-doc, opum-fleet, opum-marketplace, opum-web, quest-web) pass --target claude, so none is affected. (2) Invocation form, both the string agents --check and the argv form "agents", "--check", over opum-cli-e2e suites/ and lib/ at origin/dev ab19fec. The bare call sites are 10-contract-quest:381, 22-quest-bootstrap:288/320/364/380/456, 40-cross-product:829, 45-parity-backlog:632 and 50-packaging:377. I read each one: in every case either AGENTS.md carries the Quest block or no file carries one (at 40-cross-product, CLAUDE.md holds only lore markers, which the new check does not count). None changes verdict. BLIND SPOT: argv assembled dynamically from variables, and callers outside this fleet.
finalSummary: Decided and fixed ADR gap 4 (opum-doc 2112fc6). The codex default stays, because the codex managed block tells CI to run the check with no --target. The silent case, a bare --check in a project whose Quest block lives in CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md, now exits 6 naming the --target to use rather than exiting 0 about AGENTS.md. Help and the workspace guide describe it, and the guide's wrong claim that a missing block exits 6 is corrected. Verified by 4 new tests, a control that turns red exactly the 2 predicted cases, bun run check (614 pass), and a two-pass consumer sweep: no fleet CI or opum-cli-e2e call site changes verdict.
